question: A search-augmentation team wants each batched research request to use a server-side web search tool so Claude can look up current information and incorporate it into the same response, without the application fetching pages or feeding results back itself. Is this workable within the Message Batches API?
options: A) Yes, but only if the application also submits a matching synchronous request in parallel so the server tool has a live connection to execute against
B) No, because the Message Batches API rejects any request that references a tool definition, whether the tool executes on the server or on the client
C) No, because server tools only function within streamed synchronous responses and streaming is one of the parameters batch requests do not support
D) Yes, because server tools such as web search resolve automatically within the request itself, unlike client-side tools that need an application-supplied result
correct_answers: D) Yes, because server tools such as web search resolve automatically within the request itself, unlike client-side tools that need an application-supplied result
explanations: Incorrect. No parallel synchronous request is needed; the server tool executes within the batch request's own processing, independent of any other request.
Incorrect. Tool use, including server tools, is explicitly supported in batch requests; only a narrow set of parameters such as streaming are disallowed.
Incorrect. Server tools do not require a streaming connection to function; they resolve within the asynchronous batch request just as they would in a non-streamed synchronous call.

Correct. Server tools like web search execute as part of resolving the single batched request, so no application-side round trip is needed; this is distinct from client-side tools where the app must supply a tool_result to continue.
